title: Soft-spillover reservation windows for prefix-cooperative KV eviction with forward-progress invariants
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Under continuous batching, large requests and tenant bursts create transient pressure that causes aggressive eviction decisions. Current LRU/TTL heuristics can evict prefixes mid-flight or create repeated cache thrash that harms latency and quality. Additionally, GPU memory fragmentation increases when reclaim and reallocation happen non-deterministically across slots.

Goal: Implement a soft-spillover reservation window mechanism that cooperates with prefix-aware placement to guarantee forward progress (no request-induced livelock), bounded staleness for KV entries, and reduced fragmentation during reclaim. Provide deterministic correctness invariants, a test harness for injection scenarios, and telemetry to verify behavior in canary clusters.

Why unique: This ticket focuses on a cooperative, temporary reservation system (soft-spill lanes) rather than only changing eviction ranking. It explicitly ties eviction actions to progress tokens and prefixed micro-reservations so in-flight batches are never catastrophically trimmed. The work spans runtime changes, scheduler hints, and a verification suite.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Soft-spillover reservations implemented: when a prefix has active in-flight KV usage, runtime grants a short-lived reservation window (ms scale) that prevents eviction of hot entries unless memory pressure exceeds an emergency threshold.
2) Reservation semantics are prefix-cooperative: colocated requests see consistent reservation outcomes and reservations are transferable across batches via a progress token.
3) Correctness invariants documented: forward-progress (no livelock), bounded-staleness (TTL+reservation <= configured staleness bound), and atomicity of reservation grant/revoke.
4) Unit+integration fuzz harness covers: simultaneous tenant bursts, batched prefetches, forced fragmentation, and multi-GPU eviction scenarios; no assertion failures in 100k simulated traces.
5) Canary deployment in dedicated pool shows latency p50 improvement under bursty workloads and reduces eviction-induced soft-failures by >= 90% compared to baseline.
6) Telemetry dashboards show reservation hit/miss rates and reservation-induced delayed-eviction counts.
7) Design doc + API hints shipped and a short runtime-1.22 release note entry prepared.
technical_approach:
1) Reservation token: extend the runtime KV lease to include a 16-bit reservation token that ties a prefix to a soft-reservation epoch. Tokens are cheap and stored in slot metadata.
2) Grant policy: when a request touches a prefix and the KV entry is hot (accessed in last N ms or part of an active batch), grant a soft-reservation for W ms where W is adaptive based on recent batch completion latency.
3) Eviction check: eviction will consult reservation tokens and only evict reserved slots under emergency reclaim (configurable high-water mark) or after token expiry. Normal LRU/TTL heuristics still compute rank but must respect reservations.
4) Transfer and progress tokens: if a batch that holds a reservation spawns another batch (continuous batching), it can pass the reservation token to the successor batch to preserve in-flight data. Token transfer is a lock-free CAS op on the slot metadata.
5) Defragmentation-friendly deallocation: when evicting reserved slots (emergency), prefer coalescing adjacent freed slabs to reduce fragmentation; add a compact-after-evict flag so allocator can run a short compaction sweep during low activity.
6) Correctness proofs: formalize invariants in the design doc (linearizability of reservation grant/revoke relative to requests, forward progress lemma showing that at least one request from an active batch will complete within reservation+max-retry windows).
7) Policy configuration: expose parameters (W, high-water mark, adaptive window multipliers) via config and runtime flags for canary tuning.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token CAS semantics and expiry paths.
- Integration test that replays recorded production traces with bursts and validates no eviction of reserved prefixes during the reservation lifetime.
- Fuzz bench: extend existing kv-eviction-fuzzbench with reservation-aware scenarios and 100k randomized runs.
- Multi-GPU sim: synthetic test that forces fragmentation and emergency reclaim to verify compact-after-evict does not regress throughput.
- Canary: enable feature flag in stage and then one dedicated canary pool; monitor reservation metrics and tail latency.
- Load test: A/B against baseline for 48h under mixed-seq-length workloads to confirm QoS and cost impact.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag and default-off.
2) Run unit/integration/fuzz tests in CI; code owners review.
3) Enable in stage for 72h with telemetry dashboards.
4) Canary: enable in 1 dedicated pool for 7 days; collect metrics and a release checklist.
5) Progressive rollout to 10% of pools, 50%, then 100% conditional on no regressions.
6) Post-rollout: enable compact-after-evict on a per-cluster toggle and validate memory fragmentation metrics for 2 weeks.
7) If emergency regressions occur, toggle off the feature flag and fall back to previous LRU/TTL behavior (we ship a small compatibility shim to drop tokens gracefully).
